values.variable: O2 uptake, sitting in pressurized rover
values.normalization: per kg body mass (Table 4 kcal/h column reconciles with subject mass 80.7 kg)
values.limitations: Taken by Chappell from a published resting-rate study (their ref. 10, Jeng et al. 2003, Earth, unsuited), not measured in the IST series.
values.marsApplicability: low: Earth resting value, not suit-specific

values.variable: O2 uptake, suited walking during EVA
values.uncertainty: not reported in Table 4 (scatter shown in Fig. 10)

conditions.gravity: lunar (0.17 g) on POGO partial-gravity simulator
conditions.participants: IST-1 cohort (NASA/TP-2010-216115; count not verified here)

values.limitations: Average over speeds 2.3-3.5 km/h at lunar gravity; one suit (MKIII); suited VO2 inferred from CO2 production.
values.marsApplicability: low-medium: Mars 0.38 g is outside the tested range; Mars walking is expected to cost more per kg, magnitude unverified
values.permittedUse: sensitivity comparison only; never replaces the slope-dependent walking model

values.variable: O2 uptake, stationary EVA task - light work (observations, tool-free sample pickup, setup)
values.uncertainty: not reported in Table 4 (scatter shown in Fig. 11)
values.limitations: Six male astronaut subjects; MKIII only; VO2 inferred from suit CO2 and each subject's VCO2-VO2 regression (NORCROSS-2010-216125 p.10).
values.marsApplicability: medium: stationary work depends less on gravity than walking, but 0.38 g is outside the tested 0.12-0.32 g range

values.variable: O2 uptake, stationary EVA task - heavy work (hammering, trenching)
values.uncertainty: not reported in Table 4 (scatter shown in Fig. 12)

values.variable: O2 uptake, mobile EVA task - heavy work (sample transfer)
values.uncertainty: not reported in Table 4 (scatter shown in Fig. 13)
values.marsApplicability: low-medium: includes carrying, which scales with gravity

values.limitations: Small, all-male cohort; no female astronauts fit the MKIII at the time.
values.permittedUse: sensitivity ranges (body mass); demo crew VO2peak labelled ASSUMED

values.location: Section 2.6, p.10 (PDF p.25); Section 3.6, p.77-78 (PDF p.92-93)
values.value: Suit ventilation x exhaust CO2, converted with each subject's VCO2-VO2 regression; mL O2 per kg body mass per min
values.uncertainty: authors call for direct O2 measurement in future
values.limitations: Only the MKIII suit tested; varied-weight trials changed weight, not mass.

values.location: Table 4, p.13 (derived from the mL/kg/min and kcal/h columns at 80.7 kg)
values.variable: Energy equivalent of O2 implied by Table 4
values.uncertainty: derived; rows give 4.8197-4.8242 (rounding of the kcal/h column)
values.limitations: Implied by the table, not stated in the text.

values.variable: EMU operating pressure and O2 fraction
values.limitations: EMU heritage; a Mars suit set-point is not defined. CHAPPELL-2010 p.17 instead assumed 80% O2 at 4.3 psi for its consumables estimate.
values.permittedUse: ASSUMED suit set-point; DERIVED ppO2 and PIO2

values.limitations: Short-term hyperoxia 6-9 h; mild hypoxia limit is a 1-h time-weighted average with absolute floor 122 mmHg.
values.permittedUse: reference comparison of DERIVED PIO2 (no alarm logic)

values.variable: Historical EMU reference regression of suit ppCO2 on metabolic rate
values.limitations: A verification reference for EMU-heritage hardware, not a prediction for any Mars suit; output is ppCO2, not PICO2.
values.permittedUse: MODELLED, EXPERIMENTAL ppCO2 estimate for an EMU-like suit

values.limitations: Based on Shuttle/ISS EVA experience; applies to PICO2, not the ppCO2 regression output.
values.permittedUse: reference only (not compared against modelled ppCO2)

values.variable: Suited crewmember heat storage design range
values.limitations: Requires dQ computed with the 41-Node Man or Wissler model; a design requirement, not a live medical alarm.
values.permittedUse: reference only until a validated thermal model exists

values.variable: Nominal suited metabolic-rate range the heat-storage limit is designed for
values.permittedUse: reference comparison of MODELLED metabolic rate

values.location: p.6, table 'Crewmember Metabolic Rates for Suited Operations'
values.limitations: Max values are transients < 15 min; walkback test n=6, simulated 10-km lunar walk. Apollo values are secondary (original SP-368 chapter not retrieved).

conditions.suit: EMU (and Orlan data in the TB table)

values.limitations: Group regression explains 40% of variance; MR itself came from O2 tank pressure decay, which includes suit leakage. Individual calibration needed.
values.marsApplicability: low without per-crew calibration in Mars-relevant conditions
values.permittedUse: HR shown only with a per-crew calibration; no group coefficients used

values.variable: Liquid-cooled garment control concept (inlet temperature vs metabolic rate at comfort)
values.limitations: Shuttle EMU development test; controller relationships are hardware-specific.
values.permittedUse: architecture rationale only (heat removal is an explicit input, never assumed equal to production)
